newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PX50 rises for first time in eight session.
newsitem.headline: Czech PX50 rises for first time in eight session.

text.p: Czech shares rebounded on Thursday with both the major issue dominated RPIX and the broader PX50 closing higher for the first time in eight session.

In the wake of serious problems last week at the country's biggest fully private bank, Agrobanka, the PX50 declined by around five percent but analysts said the scale of the fall was not justified by fundamentals.

"The decline was really not based on fundamental changes, but events related to Agrobanka and speculation about (Finance Minister) Kocarnik and (central bank governor) Tosovsky," Daniel Gladis of Atlantik Financni Trhy told Reuters.
"I think that people will realise that what happened is actually a positive sign for the market because it is forcing a clean-up," he added.
The recovery from major issues gathered pace throughout the day, with the RPIX closing up seven points after being down one at the morning price fixing. The PX50 rose 2.5 points to 548.9.

Leading the pack was SPT Telecom, the bourse's most heavily capitalised issue, which rose 29 crowns to 3,279. Power utility CEZ also bounced back, gaining five crowns to 1,005 despite dipping below 1,000 earlier in the day.
Komercni Banka rose 23 crowns to 2,222 while Ceska Sporitelna was the only decliner among the major issues falling four crowns to 306.
